mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved for three consecutive weeks (-37.9 to -28.3). This momentum reflects accumulating consumer confidence and will persist, pushing average RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
evidence_refs: fact:three consecutive weekly increases from -37.9 to -28.3
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the trailing 28-day mean despite the prior three-week upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: Once TRANSIT mobility crosses above the -20 threshold, commuters resume routine trips that pass through retail corridors, mechanically lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -20 for at least one week and holds for the following week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -27.7 to -16.7, crossing -20 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise or declines in the two weeks following a TRANSIT crossing above -20.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates restored commuting-linked shopping behavior: workers stopping at retail outlets en route to/from work. Their joint upward movement amplifies RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series alone predicts.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than the growth predicted by either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT individually, or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint WORKPLACES/TRANSIT improvement.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in RESIDENTIAL (7.9 to 5.1) signals a policy-driven relaxation of stay-at-home measures. In such a reopening regime, freed time outside the home is redirected toward retail and recreation, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.3 at t-2w to 5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise even as RESIDENTIAL continues to decline over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility recovery (-39.0 to -28.7) reflects favorable weather/seasonal conditions drawing people outdoors. This seasonal outdoor activity spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits within one week, lifting RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved each week from -39.0 to -28.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following continued PARKS improvement, indicating no spillover effect.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility stalls or reverses week-on-week after its recent recovery, it signals a halt in commuting normalization, which will cap or reverse the RETAIL_REC recovery within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change turns negative or flat (<1 point improvement) after two consecutive weeks of gains
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved by 7.4 points between t-1w and t-0w after smaller prior gains
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next two weeks even though TRANSIT stalls or reverses.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of falling RESIDENTIAL and rising WORKPLACES indicates households are substituting in-home time for out-of-home work and errands. This combined substitution effect drives a larger RETAIL_REC increase than either series predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell while WORKPLACES rose over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rise over the next 4 weeks is no larger than what RESIDENTIAL or WORKPLACES alone would predict, or RETAIL_REC falls despite the joint pattern.

mechanism_narrative: Despite the current reopening trend, if WORKPLACES or TRANSIT suddenly drop by more than 10 points week-on-week, it signals a policy reversal (renewed restrictions), which will sharply reduce RETAIL_REC within one week due to curtailed movement.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES or TRANSIT falls by more than 10 points in a single week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -27.1 to -31.3 between t-3w and t-2w, a 4.2-point fall
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week of a greater-than-10-point drop in WORKPLACES or TRANSIT.
